node.label: Walter Johnson
node.date_label: Soul by Soul (1999) · “On Agency” (2003) · River of Dark Dreams: Slavery and Empire in the Cotton Kingdom (2013)
node.description: A historian of American slavery who interrogates the categories historians use to describe enslaved people. “On Agency” argues that treating the discovery of agency as the culmination of slavery history can reproduce liberal assumptions and obstruct attention to historically specific human experience.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Soul by Soul (1999); “On Agency” (2003); River of Dark Dreams: Slavery and Empire in the Cotton Kingdom (2013).

proposed_edges.relationship: Questions histories that make recovering agency the endpoint of interpreting slavery.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Read article, especially opening problem and closing methodological discussion; criticism is of an analytic habit rather than of enslaved action itself.

proposed_edges.relationship: Calls for historically specific accounts of enslaved humanity, action and collective life beyond the agency/resistance formula.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Read article’s distinction between humanity and agency, with its caution about liberal notions of autonomous selfhood. This is a methodological contribution to slavery history, not a claim every case has been independently verified.

verification.note: Complete twelve-page article read. Critique of agency/resistance equivalence and liberal selfhood is methodological; does not deny enslaved people acted or resisted.
